It's really hard to ELI5 the blockchain, but here is my best attempt:

  1. The blockchain itself is a running ledger of transactions. These transactions are updated every 10 minutes.
  2. Every 10 minutes every miner submits work to a complex math problem. A single miner (or, a group of miners pooling their power together) is selected as the winner for updating the ledger, and is awarded a solution reward, which is an amount of BTC. This is the primary reason people mine, and also serves to keep the ledger moving forward.
  3. Every 10 minutes the ledger grows through two means - one is official data, containing the previous 10 minutes transactions which are replicated to every single wallet in existance, and the second is an artifical complexity increase to make the next math problems solution harder to accomplish.

Some key things to understand with that knowledge:

  1. Every single transaction contains a private and a public key. You hold your own private key, and you can use your private key to make as many public keys as you wish to transact with (so, think of it like having a different bank account for paying your car, house, cell bill, etc).
  2. By the nature of being decentralized, EVERY OTHER PERSON HAS A LEDGER which contains your public keys transactions as a method of verifying the transaction existed. Think of it like every credit card in the world having a record of your credit card purchase, but without the private key there is no way of connecting the purchase itself to you or your wallet - only you hold that key, and losing it means you lose control of your account so you would never give it up.
  3. No single entity gains over 51% of the raw mining power, or the cryptography behind it allows what's known as a 51% exploit, where that entity has a majority of what should be "decentralized" and is able to simply lie to the other 49%. This is a form of brute-force control that also serves to balance out the possibility of this happening by the fact that the problems become harder to solve with every soltuion.

TL:DR; With each 10-minute ledger update, the artificial data or "noise" that is added by design to both make the next ledger update harder to accomplish as well as prevent exploitative hijacks of the decentealized network, over time the ratio of actual ledger data to white noise has become a mathematical number so stageringly difficult to appreciate that the only way I've ever been able to explain it is the train analogy.

While it's completely possible, and I would argue most likely, that this "noise" is just that - the scary thought would be if that noise was in fact being used as a form of decentralized raw processing power for either a government or private supercomputing project.. or more scarily, the evolutionary self-deveopment of a rogue AI. Given the nature, we'd never know until computing takes science-fiction level leaps (such as Quantum computing) and we were able to break the encryption and actually disect what the rest of that data does.
